questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A country town grows bigger as more families move in. What change is most likely?
choices: More houses, schools and shops are built
questions.explanation: More families need more places to live, learn and shop, so the town builds more.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: In 1960, Mr Costa moved from Italy to a country town. He opened a bakery. How did he contribute to the town?
choices: He changed the name of the town
He gave people new foods and jobs
questions.explanation: People from different backgrounds bring new foods, skills and jobs to a community.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Ella wants to learn how her suburb looked 50 years ago. What is the best way to find out?
choices: Count the houses on her street today
Ask a neighbour who has lived there for 50 years
Guess from the shops she sees now
questions.explanation: A person who lived there long ago can tell you what the suburb was really like.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Anzac Day is a day when Australians remember people who served in wars. On which date is it?
questions.explanation: Anzac Day is on 25 April each year. 26 January is Australia Day.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Each country has plants or animals that stand for it. Which plant is Australia's national floral emblem?
questions.explanation: The golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem. Its green and gold colours are Australia's national colours.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: The Aboriginal flag and the Torres Strait Islander flag are both official flags of Australia.
questions.explanation: Both flags are official flags of Australia. They show the importance of First Nations peoples.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Australia has six states and some territories. Which of these is a territory, not a state?
questions.explanation: The Northern Territory is a territory. Tasmania, Victoria and Queensland are states.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Which country lies just north of Australia, across the Torres Strait?
questions.explanation: Papua New Guinea is close to the northern tip of Queensland. New Zealand is to the south-east.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Before Europeans arrived, who looked after the land we now call Australia?
choices: One single group for the whole continent
Many First Nations groups, each with its own Country
questions.explanation: Hundreds of First Nations groups lived across Australia. Each group had its own Country.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: What does the word Country mean to First Nations peoples?
choices: Land, waters, sky and living things that people belong to and care for
Only a farm that someone owns
Only the place where a person was born
questions.explanation: Country is the land, waters, sky and all living things. People feel connected to it and care for it.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Torres Strait Islander peoples live on islands north of Queensland. Why is the sea so important to them?
choices: It gives food and a way to travel, and it is part of their stories
It is only a place to swim
It stops them leaving the islands
It is not important to them
questions.explanation: The sea gives food and travel routes. It is also part of their culture and stories.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Desert peoples and coastal peoples used different foods and tools. Why?
choices: Desert peoples did not like fish
Shops in each place sold different things
Their Countries have different plants, animals and water
questions.explanation: Each Country has its own plants, animals and water. People used what their Country gave them.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Which of these is a built feature?
questions.explanation: People built the Sydney Harbour Bridge. The others were made by nature.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Indonesia is close to the equator, so it is hot and wet for most of the year. How is southern Australia different?
choices: It is closer to the equator
It has cooler winters and four seasons
questions.explanation: Southern Australia is further from the equator. It has cooler winters and four seasons.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A school has a rule to walk, not run, on the verandah. Why?
choices: It is a game for teachers
questions.explanation: Running can cause crashes and falls. The rule keeps everyone safe.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Dogs must be kept on a lead in some parks. Who usually makes this kind of local rule?
questions.explanation: Local councils make rules for local places like parks, beaches and streets.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Ben breaks a school rule and must stay inside at lunchtime. What do we call this?
questions.explanation: A consequence is what happens when a rule is broken.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Which is a way a Year 3 student can help their community?
choices: Wait until they are grown up
Ask others to do all the work
questions.explanation: Children can help now, for example by cleaning up with others.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Many people give their time free to the local rural fire service. Why do communities need volunteers like this?
choices: Volunteers are paid more than other workers
Volunteers are the only people who can drive
Volunteers help services reach more people and keep the community safe
questions.explanation: Volunteers give their time without pay. This helps services look after more people.
